lessons.title: Non-Fiction: Materials All Around Us
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to retrieve facts about material uses from a non-fiction text.
success_criteria: I can find a fact about a material's use.
I can answer a question using the text.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model reading a non-fiction text about material uses.
lessons.independent_task: Children read an extract and answer retrieval questions.
key_questions: What is this material used for?
Where did you find that fact?

differentiation.greater_depth: Answer in full sentences using text evidence

lessons.assessment_notes: Note non-fiction retrieval skill — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Find a fact about a material at home.

lessons.title: Materials Survey: Tally and Table
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to record and interpret a materials survey.
success_criteria: I can record a tally.
I can interpret a simple table.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap data handling from earlier terms.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model conducting a survey of materials used for classroom objects, recording in a table.
lessons.independent_task: Children conduct and record a materials survey, answering questions about it.
key_questions: How many objects were made of wood?

differentiation.support: Adult supports tallying and table completion

lessons.assessment_notes: Record data handling consolidation applied to a science context — evidence for MATHS.STAT.
lessons.home_link: Do a simple materials survey at home.

lessons.title: Which Material Is Best for Which Job?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify the most suitable material for a given purpose.
success_criteria: I can name a material's property.
I can say why it's suitable for a job.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss matching material properties to purposes (waterproof for umbrellas, transparent for windows).
lessons.independent_task: Children match materials to purposes, recording reasoning based on properties.
key_questions: Why is this material suitable for this job?

differentiation.greater_depth: Match 6+ pairs and explain reasoning using specific properties

lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of material property knowledge to real-world suitability — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Think of a material and why it's good for its job at home.

lessons.title: Writing About Material Suitability
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to write sentences explaining why a material is suitable for a purpose.
success_criteria: I can write why a material is suitable.
I can use 'because'.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model writing a sentence explaining material suitability using 'because'.
lessons.independent_task: Children write 2-3 sentences explaining material suitability.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note explanatory writing with scientific reasoning — evidence for ENG.W2/W3.
lessons.home_link: Explain why a material is suitable for something at home.

lessons.title: Materials Arrays: Multiplication
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to represent multiplication using arrays of material samples.
success_criteria: I can create an array.
I can write the multiplication sentence.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model creating arrays using material sample squares (e.g. 3 rows of 4 fabric swatches).
lessons.independent_task: Children create arrays using material samples and write matching multiplication sentences.

differentiation.support: Create arrays for 2 and 10 times tables
differentiation.greater_depth: Create arrays for 2, 5 and 10 times tables

lessons.assessment_notes: Record array representation of multiplication, applied cross-curricular — evidence for MATHS.N3.
lessons.home_link: Find an array of objects at home and write the multiplication sentence.

lessons.title: Comparing Material Properties in Detail
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to compare a wider range of material properties.
success_criteria: I can compare two materials using 3+ properties.
I can decide which is more suitable overall.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap material properties known (hard, soft, waterproof, transparent, flexible).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model comparing two materials across multiple properties for an overall suitability judgement.
lessons.independent_task: Children compare two materials across 3+ properties, concluding which is more suitable for a purpose.

differentiation.greater_depth: Compare using 4+ properties and justify conclusion

lessons.assessment_notes: Note deeper comparative reasoning about materials — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Compare two materials at home using multiple properties.

lessons.title: Phonics: Reading Material Words
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to blend and read material-themed words.
success_criteria: I can read material words.
I can read a sentence about materials.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Reinforce a spelling pattern, applying it to material-themed words (e.g. 'plastic', 'metal', 'fabric').
lessons.independent_task: Children read themed word and sentence cards.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note phonics/spelling application — evidence for ENG.R1.
lessons.plenary: Celebrate reading progress with a themed reading game.
lessons.home_link: Practise reading material words over the week.

lessons.title: Materials Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to solve addition/subtraction word problems using a materials context.
success_criteria: I can solve an addition problem.
I can solve a subtraction problem.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap addition and subtraction strategies to 100.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Model solving word problems using a materials context (e.g. fabric squares used in a project).
lessons.independent_task: Children solve materials-themed word problems within 100, showing working.
lessons.assessment_notes: Record word problem solving skill — evidence for MATHS.N2.
lessons.home_link: Make up a materials word problem for your family.

lessons.title: Why Not Use Glass for a Football?
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to explain why an unsuitable material choice would cause problems.
success_criteria: I can say why glass is unsuitable for a football.
I can suggest a better material.
lessons.starter_activity: Discuss silly material choices (a glass football, a paper umbrella).
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss why unsuitable materials cause problems, linking to properties.
lessons.independent_task: Children identify problems with silly material choices and suggest better alternatives.
lessons.assessment_notes: Note application of material property knowledge through humour/problem-solving — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.plenary: Recap silly material choices and better alternatives.
lessons.home_link: Think of a silly material choice and a better one with your family.

lessons.title: Materials Detective Presentations
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to present a material comparison clearly to the class.
success_criteria: I can present my comparison.
I can answer a question about it.
lessons.starter_activity: Recap material comparisons made this week.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss what makes a clear presentation of a scientific comparison.
lessons.independent_task: Children present their material comparison to a small group, answering a question.
key_questions: Which was more suitable and why?

differentiation.greater_depth: Present unprompted with confidence and detail

lessons.assessment_notes: Note spoken language and scientific reasoning presentation — evidence for ENG.SL1/SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Present your material comparison to your family.

lessons.title: 3D Shapes and Their Materials
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to identify materials used to make different 3D shapes.
success_criteria: I can name a 3D shape.
I can say what material it's often made from.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Discuss common materials used for different 3D shaped objects (glass spheres, wooden cubes).
lessons.independent_task: Children match 3D shapes to common materials, recording their matching.
key_questions: What material is this 3D object made from?
Why might it be made from that material?
lessons.assessment_notes: Note cross-curricular shape and material application — evidence for MATHS.GEO/SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Find 3D shaped objects at home and name their material.

lessons.title: Uses of Materials Quiz: Reading Comprehension
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to answer comprehension questions about material uses.
success_criteria: I can answer a retrieval question.
I can answer an inference question.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Read a summary passage about material uses, modelling retrieval and inference questions.
lessons.independent_task: Children answer a mix of retrieval and inference questions about the passage.
key_questions: What is this material used for?
Why wouldn't glass be good for a football?

differentiation.support: Answer retrieval questions with text pointing

lessons.assessment_notes: Note comprehension progress — evidence for ENG.R2.
lessons.home_link: Quiz your family on material facts you learned.

lessons.title: Maths Review: Arrays, Data, Word Problems
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to apply array, data handling and word problem skills learned this week.
success_criteria: I can create and use an array.
I can read a data table.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap of arrays, data handling, and word problems.
lessons.independent_task: Children rotate through 2 stations: arrays/multiplication, data handling.
lessons.assessment_notes: Summarise week 16 maths observations for each child — evidence for MATHS.N3/STAT.
lessons.plenary: Class recap game combining both skills.
lessons.home_link: Continue practising times tables over the weekend.

lessons.title: Uses of Everyday Materials Topic Recap
lessons.learning_objective: Children will be able to summarise key learning about material uses and suitability.
success_criteria: I can name a material and its use.
I can explain material suitability.
lessons.main_teaching_input: Quick recap quiz format covering material uses, properties and suitability.
lessons.independent_task: Children complete a review worksheet and contribute to a class 'Uses of Everyday Materials' display.
key_questions: What have we learned about materials?

differentiation.support: Word bank and picture support provided

lessons.assessment_notes: Note material suitability understanding progress, setting up shape-changing next week — evidence for SCI.MAT.
lessons.home_link: Share what you learned about materials with your family.
